summary_out.outcome: pnl +6304.05% vs simple baseline ($2769.75 vs $43.25 over 11 apples-to-apples dates), sharpe 13.93, slippage 0.0/0.0. Gate vs simple: PASS by wide margin. summary_out.hypothesis: L2's next text proposed the natural single-step probe: raise adverse_threshold_ticks 1 -> 3, on the reasoning that 1 tick is bid-ask oscillation while 3 ticks ($0.75) is three full-spread displacements that constitute an adverse regime rather than noise. I predicted L3 would land between L2 and base on trade_count, skewed toward base, and ideally above base in pnl. The trade_count direction and the pnl direction were both correct (trade_count moved 81,034 -> 75,587 toward base's 73,802; pnl moved 2,092 -> 2,770 toward base's 3,564). The 'above base in pnl' version did NOT happen; +1,785 trade-count delta vs base is admitting reversals that are still net money-losing on average. PARTIALLY VINDICATED; the right axis with still-too-permissive a threshold.
summary_out.brief_summary: ptg-b-l3 (position-tier-gate brief-summary loop 3) raised adverse_threshold_ticks 1->3 ($0.25->$0.75 adverse-mid floor for the reversal-override). Result: PASS vs simple (+6304.05% pnl) and a substantial recovery from L2 (-41.30% -> -22.29% vs base, +19 pp), but still WORSE than base on 11/11 dates. vs L2: +32.38% pnl on -6.72% trades (-5,447 fewer reversal admits -> +$677), confirming each L2-admitted reversal at 1 tick was on average money-losing. vs base: still +1,785 trade-count delta -> the override is still admitting net-loss reversals. Hypothesis PARTIALLY VINDICATED: the right axis (signal-strength via adverse mid), correctly tightened direction, but threshold still too permissive. Convex monotonic L1->L2->L3 trajectory (-75.33%, -41.30%, -22.29% vs base) with decreasing marginal returns is exactly what the L2 next text described as the in-flight diagnostic for the +trade_count branch.
summary_out.next: Raise adverse_threshold_ticks from 3 to 5 ($1.25 in price, five full-spread displacements). L2's next text was explicit: 'if L3 still has +trade_count vs base, the predicate is still admitting too many reversals and L4 should test 5 ticks.' L3 has +2.42% trade_count vs base, so that branch fires. 5 ticks demands a meaningfully larger adverse regime than 3 ticks -- empirically, a position 5 ticks underwater is likely on the wrong side of a real micro-trend rather than oscillating. In-flight diagnostic for L4: if pnl improves further with trade_count within ~+1% of base, predicate calibration is closing on optimum. If at 5 ticks trade_count drops *below* base (gate too strict, collapsing to ~no admitted reversals) or pnl regresses, L5 should bracket back to 4. If pnl is still below base at 5 ticks with +trade_count, the adverse-mid proxy is exhausted as a conditioning variable -- L5 should pivot to a different axis (signed aggressor imbalance, spread vs rolling median, hold-time floor on reduce-only). Avoid: any return to age-only filters; any threshold below 3; any change other than the threshold constant (to preserve the clean single-axis sweep).
